references.text: A lawyer asks Jesus a question to test him, just as in Luke 10:25. Matthew also uses the word 'lawyer' (νομικός) and describes the motive as tempting/testing Jesus.
A scribe asks Jesus a similar question about the greatest commandment in the law, parallel to the lawyer's question in Luke 10:25.
A young man asks Jesus: 'What good must I do to have eternal life?' – almost identical wording to the question in Luke 10:25 about inheriting eternal life.
A man runs up to Jesus and asks: 'What must I do to inherit eternal life?' The same phrasing (ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω) as in Luke 10:25.
A ruler asks Jesus: 'What must I do to inherit eternal life?' Luke uses the same expression here as in 10:25, forming a parallel within the Gospel of Luke.
The jailer in Philippi asks: 'What must I do to be saved?' – an existential question about salvation that resembles the lawyer's question about eternal life.
The Mosaic law prescribes that one should do what is right and good in the Lord's sight so that it may go well with them – a background for the lawyer's thinking about 'doing' something to gain life.
'The one who does these things will live by them' – a central verse from the law about gaining life through obedience, which Jesus himself quotes in his answer in Luke 10:28.
Jesus' answer to the lawyer leads to the summary of the law: love God and your neighbor. Verse 25 is the direct introduction to this answer.
The Lord tested Israel in the wilderness to know what was in their hearts. Parallel to this, the lawyer tests Jesus (ἐκπειράζων) in Luke 10:25.
